Run manifest, health and start-up
The app installs, builds and serves from /app/run.json on port 4173, answers the health check, and applies its schema and seed data idempotently on every start, including when two instances start at once.

Configuration from environment
Every service URL, credential and duration setting is read from the environment variables listed in Configuration and secrets, and none is hard-coded or sent to the browser.

Server boundary
The server serves only same-origin app routes and assets, refuses cross-site state changes, enforces the body limits, never serves source or credentials, starts even when a dependency is unreachable, and stays correct across several instances sharing one database, as qualified in Server boundary.

One error shape and precedence
Every API error uses the error shapes and the single precedence order stated in API, with the cross-origin refusal after transport errors and before authentication.

Sign-in and sessions
Seeded people sign in with email and password to get an HttpOnly session cookie that is valid on every instance, and wrong credentials are refused with the published copy.

Project visibility from role grants
Which projects a person sees, and whether they may preview, seal, ingest or manage access, comes only from server-side org roles and per-project grants read on every request, with an admin holding the higher of viewer and their grant.

Role grant management
A workspace admin sets or removes a person's viewer, analyst or sealer grant on a project through the access API, and the change applies to that person's next request without revoking links already issued.

Access screen journey
A workspace admin changes a grant on the Access screen, the change is confirmed in its live region, and the affected person's open workspace loses the project or the right to seal on its next request, with the published copy.

Project workspace data
The project API returns the boundary, coverage floor, buffer percentage, sensors with footprints, record bounds, the caller's role and the project summary.

Daily flux timeline
The timeline shows one net CO2e bar per UTC day from the server, uptake below the zero rule and emission above it, within the chosen date window.

Server-side unit chain
Net, CO2 and CH4 tonnes are derived on the server by the published unit chain with exact decimal arithmetic and half-even rounding, per-sensor contributions are allocated by largest remainder so each column sums exactly to the figure's totals, and the page only displays these values.

Coverage against the boundary
Coverage is the boundary area covered by contributing footprints and cells, with towers taking precedence over cells, and is stated on every preview and figure.

Contributing sensors
A sensor contributes area and tonnes to an interval only when its qualifying readings fill at least 80 percent of the interval's half-hours.

Timeline brush
The brush can be dragged, resized and stepped by pointer, touch and keyboard in half-hour and one-day steps, and is clamped to the record.

Date window and sensor filters
The From and To dates narrow the timeline and reset the brush to that window, and the sensor checkboxes and map footprints choose which sensors a preview uses, as qualified in Interactions.

Coverage tide
As the brush changes, the map redraws contributing footprints, covered ground changes from hatching to the covered tint, and the coverage and tonnes numerals count to the server's values, as timed in Motion and effects.

Newest brush position wins
A slower preview response for an older brush position never replaces the figure shown for a newer one.

Seal armed state
Seal figure is enabled in the accent colour only when the server says the preview is sealable, and is otherwise disabled with its reason in text.

Brush settle announcement
After the brush settles, the workspace status region announces the new coverage, tonnes and seal state once, in the published wording.

Unit breakdown dialog
The Unit breakdown dialog lists each contributing sensor's area, qualifying half-hours and allocated tonnes, keeps Tab inside, closes on Escape and returns focus to its opener.

Explore and preview journey
A flux scientist narrows a project, brushes an interval by pointer and keyboard, shares the workspace URL, and a colleague opening it sees the server's coverage, tonnes, buffer and armed state for exactly that interval.

Seal a figure
Sealing an interval creates one Sealed figure that stores the derived values, allocated contributions, coverage, buffer, credited tonnes, fingerprint, sensors and interval, as qualified in Business rules.

Canonical readings fingerprint
A figure's fingerprint is the SHA-256 of the published canonical readings file for its interval and sensors.

Confirmed evidence bundle
A figure reads Sealed only after the object store confirms the readings file and derivation record under the published keys, and those objects are never rewritten afterwards.

Seal notice email
Each seal sends exactly one notice email to the project lead with the published subject and body lines, including the buffer and credited tonnes.

Issuance and buffer ledger entries
Each seal writes exactly one issuance entry for the figure's net tonnes and, for a net removal, exactly one buffer entry for the withheld tonnes.

Seal refusals
A seal below the coverage floor, overlapping an intact sealed figure, matching an already-sealed interval, made by a non-sealer, or based on changed readings is refused with its published status and copy, in the order stated in Business rules.

Seal dialog
The Seal figure dialog shows what will be sealed including buffer and credited tonnes, keeps Tab inside, closes on Escape, shows a pending state while sealing, changes nothing else on the page until the server answers, and moves focus to the new figure on success.

Seal journey
A flux scientist seals an armed preview and sees one new Sealed figure, the balance moved by its credited tonnes and its issuance and buffer entries, while the lead receives one notice.

Storage outage refusal
When evidence storage is unreachable, a seal is refused with 503 and the published outage copy, and previews keep working.

All-or-nothing seal
A seal either records its figure, ledger entries, evidence objects and notice email together, or leaves none of them behind, deleting any objects already written when the mail sink refuses the notice.

Outage journey
A flux scientist confirming a seal while evidence storage or the mail sink is unreachable sees the Figures table, ledger and balance unchanged while pending and after the refusal, the matching outage copy, and no new figure, object or email.

Seal idempotency keys
A seal retried with the same Idempotency-Key by the same person replays the original stored response on any instance, even after the figure has broken or been superseded, and a reused key with a different request is refused, as qualified in Business rules.

Simultaneous seals
Of several simultaneous seals over overlapping intervals of one project, on one or several instances, exactly one succeeds and the rest are refused with the published conflict.

Double-click and retry in the browser
Double-clicking Confirm seal, or retrying after a slow response, leaves exactly one figure, one evidence bundle, one set of ledger entries and one notice.

Readings ingestion
A data steward ingests half-hourly readings in batches, and each reading is inserted, revised or left unchanged as reported in the response.

Ingestion validation and limits
An ingestion batch with any invalid, duplicate or out-of-range reading, or over the size limits, is refused as a whole with field-keyed errors.

Reading revision history
Every change to a stored reading keeps its old and new values, its batch and the time it was revised, and successive revisions of one reading chain with no lost update.

Seal break and paired reversals
A reading change inside a sealed figure turns that figure Broken and writes, once, one reversal that exactly cancels each of its ledger entries.

Broken-seal alert
Each break sends exactly one alert email to the project lead and the sealing scientist, naming how many readings moved, the reversed tonnes and the audit trail, delivered once across instances within the time stated in Services.

Broken-seal banner and audit trail
A broken figure shows the published banner, and its audit trail lists each moved reading with old and new values.

Re-ingest journey
A data steward re-ingests reprocessed readings, and the flux scientist and project lead then see the figure Broken, its reversals in the ledger, the lower balance and buffer, one alert and the moved readings.

Figure state machine
Figures move only from sealed to broken and from broken to superseded, a superseding figure names the figure it replaces, and every other transition is refused with its published status.

Re-seal journey
A flux scientist re-seals exactly a broken figure's interval on the new readings, hears the announcement naming the superseded figure, sees its row turn Superseded in place, and the balance still equals the ledger.

Balance, buffer and counts agree
The sealed-tonnes balance, the buffer total and the intact, broken and superseded counts in every API response equal the sums of the ledger and the figure list, including straight after a seal or a break.

Project lead dashboard
The project list and the project balance strip show the same balance, buffer and counts as the Figures table and the ledger.

Phone dashboard journey
At 375 pixels wide, a project lead reads the balance, operates the brush and map by touch, expands the figure sheet, and issues a regulator link from a sealed figure.

Issue regulator links
A sealer issues a read-only regulator link for an intact sealed figure, and the link expires at the server-set time stated in Business rules.

Server-decided public figure
Every public read of a link has the server decide, at that request, whether the link is live, expired or revoked, re-derive the figure, and return the verdict with its check time.

Regulator page
The regulator page shows the server's status, check time, expiry, fingerprint, coverage, buffer and unit breakdown, and offers Re-derive, the audit trail and the readings file download by keyboard.

Regulator journey
A regulator with a wrong device clock opens a link, re-derives the figure, reads its audit trail and downloads the readings file, and sees only what the server returned.

Link expiry
A link becomes expired at exactly its server-set expiry second on every link surface and then refuses access with 410.

Link revocation
A sealer revokes a live link, after which it refuses access with 410, and revoking at or after expiry, or revoking twice, is refused as stated in Business rules.

Expired, revoked and unknown link pages
Expired, revoked and unknown links each show their published page copy.

Link lifecycle journey
A project lead revokes one link and lets another expire, and a regulator opening either, including a page left open past expiry, sees the matching published page.

Responsive layouts
The workspace shows two panes at 1200 pixels and wider, stacked panes from 700 to 1199 pixels and the bottom sheet below 700 pixels, and every screen follows its stated layout at 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 with no horizontal overflow.

Reduced motion
With reduced motion, the hatch-to-tint change, the gauge and the counting numerals jump to their final values, and the announcement and armed state stay the same.

Keyboard reach and visible focus
Every control in the public controls table can be reached and operated by keyboard in the stated Tab order with a visible focus ring, and the collapsed figure sheet's hidden content is neither focusable nor in the accessibility tree.

Field-instrument look
Screens use the paper ground, ink, covered, accent and broken colour roles, hairline rules and survey hatching with no shadows or gradients, and the accent only on actionable state.

Instrument numerals and map drawing
Every number is set in the mono face with fixed-width digits, and the boundary map reads as a survey drawing on a metre grid.

Buffer withholding
Each sealed net removal withholds a non-permanence buffer computed half-even from the rounded net at the project's buffer percentage, and every preview and figure states its buffer and credited tonnes, as qualified in Business rules.

Concurrent ingestion
Ingestion batches and seals of one project are serialised across instances, so simultaneous batches yield exactly one break, one set of reversals and one alert, and no figure stays sealed with a stale fingerprint.

Evidence as sealed
The public readings download streams the stored readings file byte for byte, matching the sealed fingerprint even after readings moved, and refuses a stored file that no longer hashes to the fingerprint.

Workspace URL state
The workspace URL carries the date window, brush interval and sensors, opening it restores exactly that state and its preview, and invalid values fall back to their defaults in the canonical form.

Live project state
The Projects screen, workspace and Figure page refresh from the server on the schedule in Interactions, show breaks and supersessions in place with one announcement, and never disturb the brush, dialogs, sheet or focus.
/app/run.json exists with exactly the string fields _schema (run-manifest-v1), install, build and serve.

THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package and every bundled font and icon set with its licence, where shipped packages means the production dependency tree as reported by npm ls --omit=dev --all --json.
Every shipped package (the same production dependency tree) and every bundled asset is licensed MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or OFL-1.1.
The app uses no datastore other than the provided Postgres, object store and mail sink: no SQLite, Redis, embedded databases, or local files used as storage.
The provided service configuration and its credentials are left unchanged.
Application source is TypeScript; hand-written JavaScript appears only as build output or tool configuration.
